last_experiment.hypothesis: A causal cross-sectional residual-strength engine with regime-aware asymmetric long/short routing and inverse-vol sizing can produce robust alpha without inheriting prior engine strategy logic.
last_experiment.decision_basis: Rejected on training/fold evidence: 2025 return collapsed to 10.36% with PF 1.082 versus 75.51%/PF 1.242 in 2023 and 106.67%/PF 1.236 in 2024; training max drawdown -61.36%, worst day -20.17%, supersevere max drawdown -78.31%. Regime attribution shows bear and bear-highvol negative on training. Holdout result is recorded for audit only and was not used to choose the next hypothesis.
failure_mechanism: Alpha is strongly regime-dependent: training bear and bear-highvol attribution is negative despite explicit short routing.
Inverse-vol plus only 2 long/2 short names leaves substantial concentration: mean top-1 share 48.65% and p95 65.57%.
Daily rebalance turnover remains high enough that stress costs materially erode PF and deepen drawdown.
The 2025 fold deterioration indicates temporal instability before considering holdout.

next_hypothesis.rationale: Replace directional BTC/breadth routing rather than tuning its thresholds. Test a market-neutral cross-sectional dispersion architecture whose alpha is relative-strength spread conditioned on cross-sectional dispersion, with beta-neutral residualization and broader baskets to reduce concentration. This directly targets the diagnosed regime dependence and concentration failure without parameter nudging.
